title: Munich museums: 30 works across three collections
subtitle: From Dürer and Rubens to Van Gogh, Münter and Kandinsky: a collection guide spanning the Alte Pinakothek, Neue Pinakothek and Lenbachhaus.
introduction: This guide follows thirty works across three Munich collections. The first ten belong to the Alte Pinakothek, the next ten to the Neue Pinakothek, and the final ten to the Lenbachhaus. Compare the self-portraits, the changing uses of colour and the ways figures inhabit a setting. The grouping follows collection ownership, not a single walk through open galleries.
visitNote: The Neue Pinakothek is closed for renovation at the time of this guide’s check. Selected works from its collection are shown elsewhere, including the Alte Pinakothek and Sammlung Schack; verify the current location of each work with the museum. Consult the Lenbachhaus separately for its displays. None of the thirty entries is a promise of current availability.

books.title: Concerning the Spiritual in Art
books.author: Wassily Kandinsky; translated by M. T. H. Sadler
books.note: An artist’s argument about colour and form. Read it alongside the Kandinsky works as a primary historical text, rather than as a key that fixes every painting’s meaning.

books.title: Über das Geistige in der Kunst
books.author: Wassily Kandinsky
books.note: The German text of Kandinsky’s discussion of colour, form and artistic aims. It is a useful companion to the English translation and to the works in the Lenbachhaus selection.

books.title: Histoire de Édouard Manet et de son oeuvre
books.author: Théodore Duret
books.note: An early account of Manet and his work, useful for the historical reception of modern French painting. Its period judgements and attributions should be read alongside current museum research.

selectionNote: An independent Artline selection of documented collection works, not an official museum ranking or a promise that every work is currently on display. Dates and qualified attributions follow the cited object evidence. Images retain their source credits.

works.title: Self-Portrait in a Fur-Trimmed Robe
works.medium: Paint on limewood; binder not specified in reviewed record
works.credit: © Bayerische Staatsgemäldesammlungen – Alte Pinakothek München. Albrecht Dürer, Selbstbildnis im Pelzrock, 1500. https://www.sammlung.pinakothek.de/de/artwork/Qlx2QpQ4Xq CC BY-SA 4.0; compressed study reproduction.
works.description: Dürer faces the viewer almost symmetrically, with long hair framing his face and one hand touching the fur of his robe. Against the dark ground, the face, fingers and individual strands of hair become unusually distinct. The inscriptions share the space on either side of his head.
works.importance: The frontal arrangement gives a self-portrait the gravity more often associated with a sacred image. Its importance lies partly in that claim for the status of the artist. Look closely at the fur and hair as well: the intellectual ambition is inseparable from the demonstration of painterly control.

works.title: The Crucifixion
works.credit: Giotto di Bondone. The Crucifixion. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Christ's body hangs against a gold ground, surrounded by angels and grieving figures. Giotto gives the people at the foot of the cross varied gestures and directions of attention. The scene remains hierarchically organised, but grief is communicated through recognisable bodily actions.
works.importance: The work offers a starting point for the guide's long history of the figure. Gold establishes a sacred field, while weight, gesture and grouping give the event a human dimension. Compare those means with Titian's darker, more turbulent treatment of Christ's suffering later in the sequence.

works.title: Saints Cosmas and Damian Saved
works.catalogueTitle: Saint Cosmas and Saint Damian Salvaged
works.credit: Fra Angelico. Saint Cosmas and Saint Damian Salvaged. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/fra-angelico/saint-cosmas-and-saint-damian-salvaged-1440
works.description: Fra Angelico distributes the story across a brightly coloured landscape and architectural setting. Groups of figures appear at different points, connected by paths, changes of level and repeated gestures. The small scale rewards a slow search for the sequence of actions.
works.importance: This narrative panel demonstrates how a single painted field can contain more than one moment. Its clarity depends on careful organisation rather than on a single dominant figure. It provides a useful contrast to the concentrated encounter in Antonello's Virgin of the Annunciation.

works.title: Virgin of the Annunciation
works.credit: Antonello da Messina. Virgin of the Annunciation. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: A woman in a dark blue mantle looks up from an open book, her hands crossed before her chest. Antonello places her close to the picture's edge, with little surrounding detail. The light on her face and fingers makes the small changes of pose unusually legible.
works.importance: The religious encounter is concentrated into a human response. Instead of supplying a large setting, the painting makes the viewer attend to face, gesture and the interruption of reading. Its economy provides a strong counterpoint to the multi-episode narrative in Fra Angelico's panel.

works.title: Madonna of the Curtain
works.credit: Madonna della Tenda. WikiArt; Raphael. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Raphael gathers the Virgin and children into a close arrangement of faces, hands and turning bodies. A dark curtain helps frame the group, while the child's upward gaze draws the viewer back towards the Virgin. The figures overlap without losing the clarity of their individual poses.
works.importance: The painting shows how affection can be made visible through composition. Its significance here is the balance between natural-looking contact and a carefully organised group. Compare the meeting of hands and eyes with the more frontal, isolated figure in Antonello's panel.

works.title: The Crowning with Thorns
works.credit: Titian. Crowning with Thorns. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Christ sits amid figures whose poles and arms cross the dark interior. Titian's broken, mobile paint makes flesh, cloth and shadow appear to merge at some edges. The strong diagonals converge on a body that remains comparatively still.
works.importance: The painting is an important example of how handling can shape the meaning of a scene. Violence is carried by the agitated surface and crossing lines as well as by the subject. Its late manner offers a striking comparison with Raphael's smoother, more clearly bounded figures.

works.title: The Great Last Judgement
works.medium: Paint on canvas; binder not specified in reviewed record
works.credit: © Bayerische Staatsgemäldesammlungen – Alte Pinakothek München. Peter Paul Rubens, Das Große Jüngste Gericht, um 1617. https://www.sammlung.pinakothek.de/de/artwork/Dj4mkQbL5A CC BY-SA 4.0; compressed study reproduction.
works.description: Bodies rise and fall through an immense vertical composition. Rubens places the commanding figures above, while the lower part fills with a dense accumulation of limbs, torsos and movement. Light and colour help separate the competing currents within the crowd.
works.importance: The picture demonstrates the capacity of a large altarpiece to organise many bodies into a legible drama. Looking only at individual figures can be overwhelming; step back and follow the major directions first. Scale is central to its effect and cannot be fully reproduced in a small image.

works.title: The Hippopotamus and Crocodile Hunt
works.credit: Peter Paul Rubens. Hippopotamus and Crocodile Hunt. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Horses rear above a tightly packed struggle between hunters and animals. Rubens makes diagonals cross through the centre, where bodies and weapons are difficult to disentangle. Bright fabric, pale flesh and dark hides create points of contrast within the crowded action.
works.importance: This painting is a concentrated study of movement, collision and pictorial compression. It belongs beside the Last Judgement because similar skills serve a very different subject. The hunt is a constructed spectacle, and the image should not be treated as a straightforward record of animal behaviour.

works.title: The Risen Christ
works.credit: Rembrandt van Rijn. Christ Resurrected. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: A half-length figure faces the viewer, with a light cloth opening across the chest. Rembrandt uses a dark surrounding space to bring the face, hair and exposed body forward. The gesture towards the torso gives the quiet pose its narrative significance.
works.importance: The image condenses a religious subject into the presence of a single body. Compare it with the young self-portrait nearby: in both, light and shadow shape recognition, but they serve different purposes. The catalogue's title and the source's alternative wording refer to this specific reproduced work.

works.title: Self-Portrait as a Young Man
works.medium: Paint on oak; binder not specified in reviewed record
works.credit: © Bayerische Staatsgemäldesammlungen – Alte Pinakothek München. Rembrandt (Harmensz. van Rijn), Jugendliches Selbstbildnis, 1629. https://www.sammlung.pinakothek.de/de/artwork/y7GE1PmGPV CC BY-SA 4.0; compressed study reproduction.
works.description: Rembrandt turns his head towards the light, leaving much of the face in shadow beneath unruly hair. The white collar and a few lit curls stand out against a restrained background. The uneven visibility makes looking itself part of the encounter.
works.importance: The painting uses the artist's own face to investigate light, surface and expression. Its importance becomes clearer beside Dürer's formal self-portrait: the two works construct artistic identity through very different poses and degrees of clarity, without either being merely an unmediated likeness.

works.title: Sunflowers
works.credit: © Bayerische Staatsgemäldesammlungen – Neue Pinakothek München. Vincent van Gogh, Sonnenblumen, 1888. https://www.sammlung.pinakothek.de/de/artwork/Y0GR9B7LRX CC BY-SA 4.0; compressed study reproduction.
works.description: A bunch of sunflowers fills a vase against a blue-green background. Van Gogh distinguishes open blooms, seed heads and curling petals through changes of shape and paint. The yellow tabletop and vessel connect the flowers to the lower part of the canvas.
works.importance: This is one particular painting in the sunflower sequence, and its colours and arrangement matter. The image shows how a still life can sustain variation within a narrow family of hues. Follow individual flower heads to see how repetition creates differences rather than a uniform pattern.

works.title: Monet in His Studio Boat
works.credit: Édouard Manet. Monet in his Studio Boat. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/edouard-manet/monet-in-his-floating-studio-1874
works.description: Manet shows Monet working inside a small covered boat, with another figure nearby. Dark structural lines frame pale clothing and patches of water, while the surrounding river remains loosely painted. The craft is both a subject in the scene and a place for making pictures.
works.importance: The work connects the practice of painting outdoors with an image of a fellow artist at work. It is especially useful beside the landscapes in this guide: the conditions of observation become visible. The brisk handling also gives the picture a character distinct from a formal studio portrait.

works.title: The Poor Poet
works.credit: Carl Spitzweg. The Poor Poet. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: A man lies propped up in a cramped attic beneath an open umbrella. Books, papers, clothing and the small stove crowd the room, while the sloping roof presses down on the figure. Spitzweg builds the scene from exact, quietly comic details.
works.importance: The painting examines the image of the impoverished artist through an interior that is both practical and absurd. The Munich museum dates its version to 1839; this guide follows that object record. Other versions and older catalogue dates should not be treated as interchangeable evidence.

works.title: The Gazebo
works.credit: The Gazebo. WikiArt; Caspar David Friedrich. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Two figures occupy a sheltered foreground, looking towards a distant church spire through climbing plants and supports. Friedrich makes the opening itself a frame within the painting. The viewer sees the landscape through the same partial enclosure as the figures.
works.importance: The painting turns looking into its subject. Distance is shaped by the foreground structure and by the figures who mediate our access to the view. Compare it with the more open roads in Pissarro and Sisley: landscape can be encountered through shelter as well as through movement.

works.title: Christ and the Samaritan Woman at the Well
works.catalogueTitle: Christ and the Samaritan woman at the well
works.credit: Angelica Kauffman. Christ and the Samaritan woman at the well. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Two seated figures face one another across a well. Kauffman gives their hands clear, complementary gestures, while the contrasting colours of their clothing separate their roles in the conversation. A restrained landscape leaves room for the encounter to remain central.
works.importance: The biblical episode is presented as a structured dialogue. Its clarity makes the painting useful for studying how gesture can carry a narrative without a crowded cast. It also extends the guide's account of history painting through Kauffman's measured arrangement of bodies and space.

works.title: A Beer Garden in Munich
works.credit: Max Liebermann. Beer Garden in Munich. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: People sit closely together beneath trees whose trunks divide the scene. Liebermann lets patches of sunlight break across clothing, furniture and ground, while the dense gathering continues into the background. Individual actions emerge gradually from the crowd.
works.importance: Modern leisure becomes a subject for sustained observation. The painting's interest lies in the relationship between a public social space and the fragmentary play of light. Compare the collective setting with Manet's smaller group on the boat: both place people within contemporary outdoor life.

works.title: Children with a Goldfish Bowl
works.credit: Paula Modersohn-Becker. Children with goldfish bowl. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/paula-modersohn-becker/children-with-goldfish-bowl-1907
works.description: A child holds a bowl near the chest within a narrow, densely coloured setting. Modersohn-Becker simplifies the figure and surrounding forms, using firm contours and broad planes rather than delicate transitions of light. The bowl provides a small, concentrated counterpoint to the body's vertical shape.
works.importance: The painting rethinks the figure through weight, contour and colour. Its importance in this sequence lies in the departure from the fleeting effects of Impressionist painting. The recorded plural title is retained; the reproduction should be examined on its own terms rather than used to invent a narrative.

works.title: A Street in Upper Norwood
works.credit: © Bayerische Staatsgemäldesammlungen – Neue Pinakothek München. Camille Pissarro, Straße in Upper Norwood, 1871. https://www.sammlung.pinakothek.de/de/artwork/PdxzrBExw5 CC BY-SA 4.0; compressed study reproduction.
works.description: A road leads between houses and a wall beneath a wide, clouded sky. Pissarro places small figures along the route, while bare branches and rooflines articulate the distance. The ordinary suburban setting is organised with the same care as a rural landscape.
works.importance: The work broadens the guide's geography and its account of modern landscape. A street, houses and everyday movement become enough to sustain the picture. Compare its cooler atmosphere with Sisley's road by the river, where the space opens in a different direction.

works.title: The Road to Hampton Court
works.credit: Alfred Sisley. The Road to Hampton Court. Image credit: Alfred Sisley. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: A broad path follows the water towards a small structure in the distance. Sisley balances the warm ground with the cooler river and sky, using small figures to establish scale. Repeated trees and banks draw the eye through the otherwise open view.
works.importance: The painting demonstrates how a simple route can organise a landscape. Its value beside Pissarro's Upper Norwood lies in the comparison: both depend on recession along a road, yet the placement of water, buildings and sky changes the experience of space.

works.title: Dance Around the Golden Calf
works.credit: Emil Nolde. Dance Around the Golden Calf. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Figures twist and leap in a compressed field of yellow, red and blue. Nolde uses forceful contours and abrupt contrasts, allowing parts of the bodies to merge with their surroundings. The dance is conveyed through the whole surface, not only through individual poses.
works.importance: The biblical subject becomes an occasion for intense colour and physical movement. Compare it with Kauffman's quieter religious dialogue: similar traditions of subject matter can support radically different pictorial languages. The painting's force does not depend on treating colour as naturalistic description.

works.title: Blue Horse I
works.credit: Franz Marc. Blue Horse I. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: A blue horse lowers its head in front of rounded, brightly coloured hills. Marc simplifies both animal and landscape, allowing their curves to echo one another. The unnatural colour separates the horse from an ordinary descriptive study while keeping its pose readily recognisable.
works.importance: The work offers a direct way into the expressive use of colour associated with the Blue Rider circle. The animal is central, but the surrounding forms participate in its rhythm. Compare the relationship between figure and setting with Münter's outdoor double portrait.
works.museum: Städtische Galerie im Lenbachhaus und Kunstbau München

works.title: Colour Study: Squares with Concentric Circles
works.catalogueTitle: Color Study: Squares with Concentric Circles
works.credit: Wassily Kandinsky. Color Study: Squares with Concentric Circles. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Twelve squares each contain a set of irregular coloured rings. Kandinsky changes the sequence and proportion of the colours from one unit to the next. Look at one circle for a moment, then move to its neighbour: a similar hue can appear different depending on what surrounds it.
works.importance: The work makes colour relationships the subject of direct experiment. It is a study, and its usefulness lies in comparison rather than in a hidden narrative. Place it beside Kandinsky's Murnau landscape to see recognisable scenery and more independent colour structures within one artistic practice.
works.museum: Städtische Galerie im Lenbachhaus und Kunstbau München

works.title: Into the Night
works.credit: Marianne von Werefkin. Into the night. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Figures move through a dark street between tall, uneven façades. Werefkin uses saturated blues, reds and violets to distinguish buildings and clothing, while the narrow passage pulls the eye into the scene. The architecture gives the walkers a strongly enclosed setting.
works.importance: The painting shows how a city scene can carry expression through colour and spatial pressure. It belongs in this guide as a distinct voice within the Munich modernist circle. Compare its street with Pissarro's open suburban road to see how differently architecture can shape movement.
works.museum: Städtische Galerie im Lenbachhaus und Kunstbau München

works.title: Jawlensky and Werefkin
works.credit: Gabriele Münter. Jawlensky and Werefkin. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Two figures rest on a green slope beneath a broad blue sky. Münter gives their clothing and hats strong outlines and clear colour areas. The tilted ground compresses the space, bringing people and landscape into a close arrangement.
works.importance: The work joins a portrait of fellow artists to an experiment in simplified landscape. Its importance lies in that combination of a named social relationship and a strong formal structure. It also provides a counterpart to the indoor conversation in Münter's Murnau painting.
works.museum: Städtische Galerie im Lenbachhaus und Kunstbau München

works.title: Kandinsky and Erma Bossi at the Table in the Murnau House
works.catalogueTitle: Kandinsky and Erma Bossi at the Table in the Murnau House
works.credit: Gabriele Münter. Kandinsky and Erma Bossi at the Table in the Murnau House. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Two people sit at a small table within a room of sharply divided colour areas. A dark wall makes the pale tabletop and faces stand out, while chairs, pictures and objects establish the domestic setting. Münter keeps the composition compact and direct.
works.importance: The painting makes an artistic circle visible through an ordinary interior. Its clarity comes from large shapes and carefully placed details rather than elaborate perspective. Compare the relationship between people and room with Manet's studio boat, another image in which an artist's environment becomes a subject.
works.museum: Städtische Galerie im Lenbachhaus und Kunstbau München

works.title: Portrait of the Dancer Alexander Sakharoff
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait of the Dancer Alexander Sakharoff
works.credit: Alexej von Jawlensky. Portrait of the Dancer Alexander Sakharoff. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: A pale face and dark hair rise above a vivid red costume. Jawlensky sets the figure against a cool background, sharpening the contrast between the eyes, mouth and surrounding colour. The turned body gives the portrait an asymmetry that prevents the frontal gaze from becoming static.
works.importance: The portrait brings performance and painting into close contact. Costume and makeup are part of the sitter's visible presentation, while the colour arrangement gives the image its force. It is a useful comparison with Dürer's self-portrait at the beginning of the guide: clothing shapes identity in both.
works.museum: Städtische Galerie im Lenbachhaus und Kunstbau München

works.title: Promenade
works.credit: August Macke. Promenade. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: People walk beneath trees whose foliage breaks into interlocking green forms. Macke repeats the verticals of bodies and trunks while varying the figures' clothing and direction. The scene remains one of public leisure, but its shallow space emphasises pattern and rhythm.
works.importance: The painting links modern outdoor life with a carefully organised surface. Compare it with Liebermann's beer garden: each treats a social gathering, but Macke makes the figures and surrounding shapes more closely interdependent. The difference is visible without reducing either work to a movement label.
works.museum: Städtische Galerie im Lenbachhaus und Kunstbau München

works.title: Murnau View with Railway and Castle
works.catalogueTitle: Murnau view with railway and castle
works.credit: Wassily Kandinsky. Murnau view with railway and castle. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/wassily-kandinsky/murnau-view-with-railway-and-castle-1909
works.description: A dark train crosses the lower part of a landscape built from bright, angular colour areas. Telegraph poles, hills and distant buildings remain recognisable, but the contrasts are stronger than a neutral description would require. The locomotive supplies a firm horizontal anchor.
works.importance: The work shows Kandinsky testing how far colour and shape can transform an observed setting while retaining its identity. It offers a useful intermediate comparison between Münter's simplified landscapes and the independent colour relationships of the concentric-circle study.
works.museum: Städtische Galerie im Lenbachhaus und Kunstbau München

works.title: Self-Portrait with a Skeleton
works.credit: Lovis Corinth. Self-portrait with Skeleton. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Corinth stands beside a skeleton in a bright studio, with large windows behind them. His clothed body and the exposed bones occupy comparable space. The direct pose and practical setting keep the encounter from becoming a purely theatrical scene.
works.importance: The skeleton is both a studio object and a reminder of mortality. That double role gives the self-portrait its particular tension. Compare it with Rembrandt's youthful study and Dürer's formal image: the guide's self-portraits use very different means to present the working artist.
works.museum: Städtische Galerie im Lenbachhaus und Kunstbau München

works.title: Improvisation: Gorge
works.credit: Wassily Kandinsky. Improvisation. Gorge. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/wassily-kandinsky/improvisation-gorge-1914
works.description: Diagonal lines, curved shapes and patches of colour crowd the surface. Some passages suggest terrain or movement, but no single viewpoint resolves the whole. Kandinsky makes the eye move between local details and larger currents across the composition.
works.importance: The painting asks for a different kind of looking from the recognisable Murnau landscape. The title offers a point of departure without functioning as a complete key. Its significance here lies in the growing independence of line and colour from a stable description of place.
works.museum: Städtische Galerie im Lenbachhaus und Kunstbau München
